newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom worth 169-195 bln FFr-CSFB.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom worth 169-195 bln FFr-CSFB.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston said on Tuesday that France Telecom SA had a "fair market value" of 169 billion francs to 195 billion francs, or 169 to 195 francs per share.
ABN Amro Hoare Govett said on Monday the company was worth between 150 and 180 billion francs and a tentative consensus seems to be as wide as 150 to 200 billion francs.
In the run-up to the partial privatisation of France Telecom beginning next month, analysts were allowed on Monday to issue studies on the company following a black-out period.

CSFB analyst Evan Miller said in a report he believed France Telecom was "very well positioned to meet the challenge of full competition from 1998 and has built a solid foundation for earnings growth beyond".
He said productivity gains from downsizing and restructuring should benefit operating margins, with de-leveraging acting to further enhance earnings per share growth.
Miller said a supportive, balanced regulatory regime "should assure the ability to complete tariff rebalancing by 2000, thus limiting competitive losses".
CSFB said it may participate in the proposed offering of France Telecom shares and could be an underwriter.
Miller said in his note he used discounted cash flow analysis (DCF), economic value analysis (EVA) and comparable company analysis to arrive at his conclusions.
He said the 1997 AMV/EBITDA (market value related to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) was an average 4.9 on a group of European telecoms companies.
He compared Deutsche Telekom AG, British Telecom Plc, KPN NV, Portugal Telecom, Telefonica, STET and Tele Danmark.

"On the basis of this 4.9 sector average, using a 1997 EBITDA figure of 58.1 billion for France Telecom, we derive an enterprise value of 285 billion francs and equity value of 178 billion," Miller said.
This implies a 1997 price/earnings ratio of 13.3 which represents a 12.5 percent discount to the sector average and an 32.1 percent discount to the French share market.
Miller said a DCF model, using an average cost of capital of 9.5 percent, found an equity value in the range of 169 billion to 195 billion francs.
With EVA, or valuing the company on the basis of projected after tax results on invested capital, the result "provides a high degree of comfort in deriving an equity valuation of 169 billion francs".
CSFB expects a France Telecom 1997 net income of 13.76 billion francs, against 13.38 billion in 1996, rising steadily to 21.4 billion francs in 2002.
